ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the following at onboarding and continuously thereafter: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation Consolidated List, FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions & Jurisdictions Under Increased Monitoring, and domestic designations under FICA and POCDATARA. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence in accordance with FICA section 28A, requiring senior management approval of the relationship, verification of source of funds and wealth, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Screening must be executed by a licensed third-party compliance data provider and documented in an audit-trail report maintained in the company's AML file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Company and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in any of South Africa's twelve official languages, but must be rendered in Latin/ASCII alphanumeric characters, without diacritics or non-Latin scripts, to be accepted by the CIPC electronic registry. The proposed name must comply with section 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and must contain the required legal suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or the accepted abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'. Names may not be offensive, misleading, falsely imply an association with the government, or conflict with a registered trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name is valid for 20 business days and may be extended once for a further 20 business days via the CIPC e-Services portal using the name reservation extension function. Upon refusal, CIPC issues written reasons; the applicant may, within 30 days of the refusal notice, apply to the Companies Tribunal for reconsideration under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, filing Form CTR 160 in accordance with the Companies Tribunal Regulations, 2011. Alternatively, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation application on Form CoR 9.1 or seek judicial review in the High Court on grounds of administrative illegality.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-service-provider address is acceptable for statutory registered-office purposes under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, provided it is a physical street address in South Africa, not a post office box, and mail-forwarding services are in place. However, for this ophthalmic pharmaceutical manufacturing scope, the commercial substance requires a separate physical aseptic production facility that must be GMP-compliant and licensed by SAHPRA; a virtual office cannot satisfy the SAHPRA site-registration requirement, and FIC/CIPC beneficial ownership filings must reflect the actual physical operating premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended, sections 13, 14, 19, 23, 66, 68 and 191
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital is prescribed; the MOI must state the authorized shares, at least one share must be issued, and the subscriber’s liability is limited to the unpaid amount on those shares. No escrow account is required under South African law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Company is duly incorporated under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 with the initial share subscriptions set out in the MOI, and each subscriber's liability is limited accordingly. 2. The registered office of the Company shall be as specified in the MOI, and the Company Secretary is instructed to file all incorporation notices with CIPC. 3. The following persons are appointed as first directors: [Names], with [CEO] as Managing Director and [CFO] as Financial Director, each holding office until the next annual general meeting. 4. The directors are authorised to open a corporate bank account, execute the tax registration, and take all ancillary actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the CoR 9.1 name reservation on the CIPC portal. Verify that the proposed name is not identical to an existing registered name and does not contain restricted words requiring ministerial approval. If the name is not reserved, select an alternative name or proceed with registration using the company's enterprise number as its name.
required_dossiers: Identity copy of the incorporator or director
Proof of residential address of incorporator (if natural person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC rejects or queries the name, file an objection within 10 business days, submit a revised name reservation, or use a company registration number as the company name and apply for a preferred name later.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI in accordance with the Companies Act, specifying the company’s incorporated legal nature, authorized share classes and rights, director powers and quorum requirements, and initial subscribers. Complete CoR 14.1 setting out the incorporators’ details, registered office, and the intended effective date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as first directors (CoR 14.2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI is defective or incompatible with the Companies Act, the CIPC will issue a query; incorporate the requisite amendments and re-submit the electronic application within 5 business days to avoid statutory fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application and Pay Prescribed Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed CoR 14.1 together with the MOI and appointing consents via the CIPC transactional portal. Pay the incorporation fee by electronic funds transfer, credit card, or debit order. The CIPC will issue a registration certificate once the application is approved.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and residential addresses of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, correct the submission within 10 business days and resubmit; if the rejection is based on non-payment, provide proof of payment. If the CIPC fails to process within statutory timelines, escalate via CIPC’s service complaint channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax and Obtain SARS Accreditation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the CIPC registration certificate, register the company for Income Tax, Value-Added Tax (if applicable), and Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) for future employees. Complete the SARS registration form electronically through eFiling, attaching the incorporation certificate. Appoint a public officer as required by tax law.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS returns a query, provide additional identifying documentation within 21 days. File a written objection with SARS if the registration status is incorrect, and request interim taxpayer status to permit importation and banking activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Appoint Auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach the chosen commercial bank with the incorporation certificate, MOI, directors’ resolutions and identification. Obtain a letter of reference from the bank after account opening. If the company meets the public interest score threshold, appoint an independent auditor and notify CIPC of the appointment.
required_dossiers: Directors’ resolution to open bank account
FICA-compliant documents and source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account for FICA non-compliance, remedy by providing enhanced due diligence documents, a shareholder introduction letter, and a structure diagram. If the auditor declines, appoint another registered auditor and file the notice with CIPC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturing Licence for Sterile Ophthalmic Medicinal Products (Category D: Aseptic Manufacture)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment (Category 15 of Listing Notice 1 of EIA Regulations; full Environmental Impact Assessment only if production capacity exceeds the defined threshold or significant mitigation is required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with National Water Act (Act 36 of 1998) water use license limits; airborne volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and particulate emissions must meet National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (Act 39 of 2004) prescribed concentration limits; hazardous waste handling must align with National Waste Management Act (Act 59 of 2008) standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate must be obtained from the relevant municipal fire brigade services, structural load inspection certificate from an accredited engineer, and workplace occupational clearance issued by the Department of Employment and Labour in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); electronic filing and registration portal: SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity or a local company with foreign ownership must first register as a taxpayer through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using Form IT77 (Company Income Tax registration) accompanied by the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of physical address, and banking details. SARS assigns an Income Tax Reference Number; if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed the VAT registration threshold, the entity must separately submit a VAT registration application (Form VAT101) to obtain a Vendor Number. Appointing a SARS-representative is mandatory for non-resident entities without a fixed place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Proprietary Limited Company is a separate South African tax resident subject to normal tax on worldwide income, without a US-style check-the-box flow-through regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not have a check-the-box election. Pty Ltd is automatically taxed at entity level at the corporate rate of 27%. Specific statutory elections exist in the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, including s 20B (trading stock valuation), s 24 (accrual/expenditure timing), s 24J (interest accrual), s 23H (prepayments), and s 25H anti-hybrid rules that recharacterise cross-border instruments to neutralise hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 (total taxable supplies made in South Africa during any 12-month period); voluntary registration permitted from R50,000 (regulation-prescribed threshold, subject to SARS discretion).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time government pre-clearance or digital stamping regime exists in South Africa. Tax invoices must satisfy the prescriptive requirements of s 20(4) VAT Act and be issued within 21 days of the supply; SARS eFiling and e@syFile are used for VAT returns and payments, not for invoice-level clearance. Electronic invoices and records are accepted if integrity and audit-trail conditions are met.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for zero-rating under s 11(1)(a) VAT Act if the exporter supplies movable goods pursuant to a sale or consignment and the goods are exported from South Africa to a foreign country by the supplier or the purchaser at the time of supply. Services qualify as exported services under s 11(2)(k) if the supply is performed outside South Africa, or is supplied directly to a non-resident who is not in South Africa and the services are not connected to fixed property or consumables in South Africa. For medical and pharmaceutical products, an export permit from the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) may be required, but zero-rating itself is not conditional on SAHPRA registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged via SARS Customs eFiling / EDI
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing goods leaving South Africa
Commercial Invoice / Tax Invoice bearing zero-rating rationale
Evidence of payment receipt from purchaser (SWIFT or Letter of Credit settlement)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorised dealer in foreign exchange where applicable
Underlying supply agreement and packing list
SAHPRA export certificate or permit where the product is listed or requires notification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may deny the zero-rating if the exporter fails to provide sufficient evidence of physical export and receipt of proceeds; the VAT becomes payable at 15% with interest (s 40) and an understatement penalty of up to 100% of the shortfall under s 223 Tax Administration Act depending on conduct (no reasonable care, substantial understatement, or intentional tax evasion). Fraudulent export claims attract criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act and Customs and Excise Act, retrospective assessments limited by law but generally five years, or longer in cases of fraud, and potential suspension of the entity's vendor registration or customs facilitation status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) and Authorized Dealers (major commercial banks) under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961; the South African Revenue Service (SARS) administers customs, export declaration validation, and tax-clearance prerequisites.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is fully convertible for current-account payments (imports, exports, dividends, interest, royalties, and services) without prior SARB approval, provided normal trade/corporate documentation and SARS records are maintained. Capital-account flows are subject to a capital flow management framework: inbound non-resident equity subscription into a ZA (Pty) Ltd is lawful at free-market rates once effected through, and recorded by, an Authorized Dealer; offshore foreign-currency accounts, outward portfolio investment, and loans to non-residents generally require FinSurv approval or an applicable AD delegation. Profit remittance is not exchange-control restricted once the inward investment record and foreign-liability reporting are complete; the operative remittance hurdles are taxation-based, principally the 20% dividends tax on non-resident shareholders (treaty relief available), dividends/interest final withholding, SARS tax clearance status, transfer pricing, and CFC rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds from sterile ophthalmic products must be received onshore through a South African Authorized Dealer within 30 days from the date of export; the AD may grant a longer period on documented commercial justification. One hundred percent of the invoice value must be repatriated into the domestic banking system; there is no fixed statutory ZAR conversion ratio, but any foreign currency must be deposited into an AD-controlled account (including an approved Foreign Currency Account) and made freely available for conversion to ZAR at market rates. Each consignment requires the applicable SARS export declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading/air waybill, customs record, and supporting quality documentation for the ophthalmic product; over-invoicing, under-invoicing, and offshore retention beyond AD-approved arrangements are exchange-control offenses.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Verto) are not licensed as South African banks and cannot lawfully act as the primary receipt and clearing account for an SARB-regulated resident exporter; receiving export proceeds directly into an unlicensed offshore EMI is incompatible with the 30-day repatriation rule and the Authorized Dealer framework. EMIs are commercially viable only as ancillary payment-orchestration, multi-currency conversion, and MT103 origination layers where the settlement owner and reporting hub remains a local AD account. Any offshore account opened by the resident company requires FinSurv approval or explicit AD facilitation; otherwise, the account is treated as an unauthorized exchange-control exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 does not statutorily compel physical attendance, but the banks' FICA/AML risk frameworks in practice require at least one director or authorized signatory to attend an in-person or live video interview with the bank's compliance officer before account activation. Fully remote onboarding is exceptional and reserved for low-risk, fully verified corporate clients using biometric identity checks and a subsequent registered-office visit; for non-resident shareholders and offshore beneficial owners, banks normally require presentation of apostilled/consularized board resolutions, notarized powers of attorney, and certified passport copies. The directors should plan for a physical Johannesburg/Cape Town appointment with the corporate banking relationship manager and a site visit to the registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque offshore beneficial-ownership chain: non-resident shareholders or intermediate holding entities present unresolved ultimate-natural-person identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Register of Beneficial Owners prepared under the Companies Act, 2008; memoranda, shareholder agreements, and group structure charts for all intermediate entities; certified identity documents/passports of all natural persons with 5% or greater interest; proof of listing or regulatory standing of the ultimate parent; and a written source-of-funds statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant inbound capital injection or late-stage loan-to-equity conversion with inadequate economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreement; board/stakeholder resolutions; SWIFT trace showing the originating account; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds certificates from the non-resident shareholder; audited parent financial statements; and the AD's foreign-liability and capital-staging record evidencing FinSurv-compliant reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade invoice anomalies in pharmaceutical exports or imports: unit-price mismatches, over/under-invoicing, or inconsistent consignee details.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Form EX/SARS export declarations and customs validation records; UCP 600 letter-of-credit documents; independent laboratory/test certificates for ophthalmic formulations; pharmaceutical benchmark pricing evidence; master batch records; bills of lading; and external audit circularization of material suppliers and buyers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions-list, or adverse-media screening hits on directors, beneficial owners, or counterparties in African distribution markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Time-stamped sanctions screening reports (UN, EU, OFAC, UK, South African targeted lists); PEP status confirmation; World-Check/Refinitiv records; directors' statutory declarations; FIC Act section 28 risk assessment; internal sanctions/compliance policy; and written AML sign-off by the bank's compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the non-resident shareholder issues a SWIFT MT103 directly to the company's South African Authorized Dealer account with a purpose designation of Direct Investment in South Africa – subscription for ordinary shares in a resident (Pty) Ltd; the AD applies the SARB FinSurv capital-liabilities transaction code for direct investment in share capital. The shareholder must provide the AD with the share allotment resolution, shareholder agreement, company registration particulars, and SARS tax-clearance evidence. Funds are staged in a restricted Capital-Staging/Provisional account until allotment documentation is lodged, after which the funds are released to the operating account in ZAR at spot or held in an FCA with AD consent. Verification requires reconciliation among the SWIFT reference, shares register, Companies Act filings, the AD foreign-liability record, and the company's annual FinSurv reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement for imported APIs, polymer tubing, blow-fill-seal consumables, and plant equipment is executed via: (i) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the AD account against verified commercial invoices, packing lists, and transport documents; and (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit (UCP 600/eUCP) issued by the AD in favor of foreign suppliers, on sight or deferred-payment terms, with inspection, insurance, and pharma-quality certificates. For SADC/SACU sales, export collections may use documentary collections (URC 522) or letters of credit received through the AD's confirmation desk. All outbound payments must identify the underlying current-account trade purpose and must not be structured as advanced settlements absent a proforma invoice and supporting SARS customs data.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (ZAR deliverable forwards) with a licensed South African Authorized Dealer in USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR, and CNY/ZAR, tenors matched to approved underlying export/import cashflows.
Vanilla deliverable FX options (puts/calls on ZAR) for the same underliers, documented under ISDA/SACMA master agreements, non-speculative, and approved by the Authorized Dealer.

Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term plant financing and refinancing of the ophthalmic manufacturing facility, subject to FinSurv underlying-debt authorization and reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only as an exception for currency crosses lacking an onshore deliverable ZAR market, such as receivables denominated in certain non-convertible Sub-Saharan African currencies, each NDF tied to a confirmed trade or loan exposure and pre-approved by the Authorized Dealer; uncovered speculative NDF positions are prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form CoR 36.1) with Beneficial Ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of registration of the (Pty) Ltd; late filing triggers CIPC late-filing penalties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC places the company in default; administrative penalties accrue until the Annual Return is filed; failure to file for two consecutive years enables CIPC to initiate deregistration under section 82 of the Companies Act 2008, resulting in loss of corporate capacity and asset vesting in the State

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SAHPRA manufacturing licence annual retention declaration and fee (ZAR-denominated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the licence anniversary or by 31 March of the SAHPRA fee year, as specified in the current SAHPRA fee schedule and licence conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment or late payment constitutes a licence compliance breach; SAHPRA may suspend or withdraw the manufacturing licence, requiring immediate cessation of aseptic manufacture of the sterile ophthalmic eye drops pending re-inspection and re-licensing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SAHPRA product registration annual retention and five-year renewal for the sterile ophthalmic eye drops
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the product registration anniversary or 31 March of the SAHPRA fee year, and renewal application before the five-year certificate expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay the annual retention fee or to renew before expiry cancels the product registration; the eye-drop product may no longer be lawfully manufactured, supplied, or marketed, and continued sale exposes the company to recall orders, administrative fines, and criminal liability under the Medicines and Related Substances Act 1965

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the company has a public interest score of 350 or more under Companies Regulation 26(2); if the Memorandum of Incorporation requires audit; if the company is a holding company or subsidiary of an audited company; or if a sectoral regulator such as SAHPRA imposes audit conditions on the manufacturing licence. A public interest score of 100 to 349 requires an independent financial review unless the owner-managed exemption applies; a score below 100 attracts no audit or review requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs is the default framework for a private (Pty) Ltd; full IFRS is required where the company is part of an audited group, elects full IFRS, or is otherwise required by the Companies Regulations 2011 and the Accounting Practices Board. Annual financial statements must be approved by the board within six months after the financial year-end.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The (Pty) Ltd must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file beneficial ownership information with CIPC upon incorporation, within 10 business days after any change in beneficial ownership, and as part of each annual return. Any shareholding transfer must be recorded in the securities register and the beneficial ownership register before the transfer is recognised by the board; a holder of 5% or more of beneficial interest constitutes a reportable beneficial owner.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 – USD 650 per year (ZAR 3,500 – ZAR 12,000) for a registered office and corporate secretarial service in Johannesburg or Cape Town
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,500 per year (ZAR 55,000 – ZAR 155,000) for a certified independent audit; an independent financial review is approximately USD 1,000 – USD 2,500 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022; stated rate reduced from 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. Preferential regimes: (a) Special Economic Zone (SEZ) 15% reduced rate for qualifying manufacturing operations; (b) s11D R&D incentive: 150% deduction for approved qualifying R&D expenditure; (c) s12I industrial project allowance: up to 35% additional allowance on qualifying building/machinery capex (greenfield) and 25% (brownfield), capped at ZAR 900m per project (with 10% labour uplift); (d) s12C accelerated wear-and-tear on manufacturing plant: 40% first-year allowance; (e) s12B renewable energy; (f) Urban Development Zone building allowance; (g) s12E small-business rate if below ZAR 20m turnover (statutory 27% headline unaffected).
